plantar metatarsal arteries: Branches running from the plantar arch to the toes.
plantar metatarsal veins: Open into the plantar venous arch.
plantar venous arch: Deep venous arch of the sole.
popliteal artery: Continuation of the femoral artery beyond the adductor hiatus; the deepest structure of the popliteal fossa, it can be injured in knee dislocation.
popliteal vein: Runs superficial to the artery in the popliteal fossa.
posterior auricular vein: Drains the area behind the ear.
posterior basal segmental artery of left: Posterior basal segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
posterior basal segmental artery of righ: Posterior basal segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
posterior branch of renal artery: Branch supplying the posterior segment; Brödel's line marks the avascular plane.
posterior cerebral artery: Supplies the occipital lobe and the inferior surface of the temporal lobe; its occlusion causes homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.
posterior circumflex humeral artery: Passes through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve and winds round the back of the surgical neck.
posterior circumflex humeral vein: Accompanies the artery of the same name.
posterior communicating artery: Links the internal carotid to the posterior cerebral artery; an aneurysm here presses on the oculomotor nerve and causes a third nerve palsy with a dilated pupil.
posterior division of internal iliac art: Posterior division of internal iliac artery
Gives the iliolumbar, lateral sacral and superior gluteal arteries.
posterior division of retromandibular ve: Helps to form the external jugular vein.
posterior inferior cerebellar artery: The largest branch of the vertebral artery; its occlusion causes the lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome.
posterior intercavernous sinus: Joins the two cavernous sinuses behind the pituitary.
posterior intercostal arteries: Branches of the thoracic aorta to the 3rd–11th spaces; run in the groove on the lower border of the rib and, enlarged in coarctation of the aorta, cause rib notching.
posterior interosseous artery: Supplies the posterior compartment of the forearm.
posterior lateral nasal branches of sphe: Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
Supply the lateral wall of the nose; the source of posterior nosebleeds.
posterior leaflet of left atrioventricul: The posterior cusp of the mitral valve; prolapse is most common in this cusp.
posterior parietal artery: Supplies the posterior part of the parietal lobe.
posterior segmental artery of left lung: Posterior segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
posterior segmental artery of right lung: Posterior segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
posterior septal branches of sphenopalat: Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
Supply the nasal septum; contribute to Kiesselbach's area.
posterior superior alveolar artery: Supplies the upper molars and the maxillary sinus.
posterior temporal branch: Supplies the back of the temporal lobe.
posterior tibial artery: Descends deep in the calf; its pulse is felt behind the medial malleolus and it passes through the tarsal tunnel to the sole.
posterior tibial veins: Accompany the posterior tibial artery; often involved in calf DVT.
posterior vein of right lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
prefrontal artery: Supplies the lateral surface of the frontal lobe.
proper hepatic artery: Rises in the hepatoduodenal ligament to the left of the bile duct and in front of the portal vein; supplies the liver and, through its right branch, the gallbladder (cystic artery).
proper palmar digital arteries: End arteries running along both sides of the fingers; this is why adrenaline in digital blocks is debated.
proper plantar digital arteries: Terminal branches running along the sides of the toes.
proximal lateral striate branches: Thin perforating branches supplying the basal ganglia and internal capsule; the source of hypertensive haemorrhages.
pulmonary trunk: Trunk leaving the right ventricle that carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs; divides under the aortic arch into the right and left pulmonary arteries.
radial artery: The artery used for the pulse at the wrist; passes through the snuffbox to form the deep palmar arch. Used for arterial blood gases and coronary angiography (Allen test).
radial collateral artery: Joins the anastomosis around the elbow.
recurrent interosseous artery: Branch that runs back to the back of the elbow.
retromandibular vein: Runs within the parotid, deep to the facial nerve.
right ascending lumbar vein: Joins the lumbar veins and continues as the azygos vein.
right atrium: Chamber receiving blood from the superior and inferior venae cavae and the coronary sinus; the sinoatrial node lies at the entry of the superior vena cava and the fossa ovalis in the interatrial septum.
right brachiocephalic vein: Short vertical vein formed by the right internal jugular and subclavian veins.
right common carotid artery: Arises from the brachiocephalic trunk; divides at the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C4) into the internal and external carotids.
right coronary artery: Arises from the right aortic sinus and runs in the right AV groove; in most people it supplies the SA and AV nodes and the posterior interventricular artery (right dominance). Its occlusion causes inferior MI and bradycardia.
right coronary leaflet: The right coronary artery arises from the sinus behind it.
right gastro-omental vein: Drains the right part of the greater curvature of the stomach.
right inferior pulmonary vein: Carries blood from the right lower lobe to the left atrium.
right inferolateral branch of right coro: Right posterolateral branch of right coronary artery
Branch of the right coronary artery to the posterolateral wall of the left ventricle.
right pulmonary artery: Branch passing behind the aorta and superior vena cava to the right lung.
right renal artery: Arises at L1–L2 and passes behind the inferior vena cava; longer than the left renal artery.
right renal vein: Short vein opening directly into the inferior vena cava.
right semilunar leaflet of pulmonary val: Right semilunar cusp of pulmonary valve
The right semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve.
right subclavian artery: Arises from the brachiocephalic trunk; passes behind scalenus anterior and becomes the axillary artery at the outer border of the 1st rib.
right subclavian vein: Continuation of the axillary vein; passes in front of scalenus anterior and is used for central catheters.
right subcostal vein: Helps to form the azygos vein.
right superior intercostal vein: Carries the right 2nd–4th intercostal veins to the azygos vein.
right superior phrenic vein: Drains the upper surface of the diaphragm.
right superior pulmonary vein: Carries oxygenated blood from the right upper and middle lobes to the left atrium.
right testicular artery: Arises from the aorta at L2 and descends in the spermatic cord to the testis.
right ventricle: Chamber forming most of the front of the heart; it has a trabeculated inner surface and a moderator band and pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk.
second posterior intercostal artery: Arises from the supreme intercostal artery.
septal branches of anterior interventric: Branches supplying the anterior 2/3 of the septum and the bundle of His.
septal branches of posterior ethmoidal a: Septal branches of posterior ethmoidal artery
Supply the upper part of the nasal septum.
septal leaflet of right atrioventricular: The cusp of the tricuspid valve facing the septum.
septal papillary muscle of right ventric: Septal papillary muscle of right ventricle
Small papillary muscle arising from the septum.
short posterior ciliary arteries: Supply the choroid and the optic nerve head.
sigmoid arteries: Two to four branches supplying the sigmoid colon.
sigmoid sinus: Curves in an S behind the mastoid and opens at the jugular foramen into the internal jugular vein; mastoiditis can cause its thrombosis.
small saphenous vein: Begins behind the lateral malleolus and opens into the popliteal vein; runs with the sural nerve.
splenic artery: The largest coeliac branch, running a tortuous course along the upper border of the pancreas; gives the short gastric and left gastro-omental branches. A posterior gastric ulcer can erode it.
splenic vein: Runs behind the pancreas; can thrombose in pancreatitis.
straight sinus: Formed by the union of the inferior sagittal sinus and the great cerebral vein (of Galen).
subcostal artery: The last segmental branch, running below the 12th rib.
submental artery: Supplies the floor of the mouth and the area under the chin.
submental vein: Drains the area under the chin.
subscapular artery: The largest branch of the axillary artery; gives the thoracodorsal and circumflex scapular branches.
superficial branch of medial plantar art: Superficial branch of medial plantar artery
Superficial branch supplying the big-toe side.
superficial dorsal veins of penis: Open into the external pudendal veins.
superficial epigastric artery: Superficial branch supplying the skin of the lower abdomen.
superficial epigastric vein: Can dilate in portal hypertension and contribute to 'caput medusae'.
superficial external pudendal artery: Superficial branch supplying the skin of the external genitalia.
superficial palmar arch: Arch formed by the ulnar artery, lying distal to the deep arch (Kaplan's line); at risk in palm injuries.
superficial temporal artery: Its pulse is felt in front of the ear; biopsied in giant cell arteritis.
superficial venous palmar arch: Accompanies the superficial palmar arterial arch.
superior anorectal artery: Continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery; supplies the upper rectum.
superior basal vein of left lung: Superior basal vein of left lung
Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
superior basal vein of right lung: Superior basal vein of right lung
Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
superior cerebellar artery: Branch of the basilar artery near its top; supplies the upper surface of the cerebellum and can cause neuralgia by touching the trigeminal nerve.
superior epigastric artery: Anastomoses in the rectus sheath with the inferior epigastric artery (a collateral path in coarctation of the aorta).
superior gluteal artery: The largest branch of the internal iliac artery, emerging above piriformis; supplies gluteus medius and minimus.
superior labial artery: Supplies the upper lip and the front of the nasal septum (contributes to Kiesselbach's area).
superior lateral genicular artery: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.
superior lingular artery of left lung: Superior lingular segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
superior lingular vein of left lung: Superior lingular vein of left lung
Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
superior lobar artery of left lung: Superior lobar artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to the superior lobe of the left lung.
superior lobar artery of right lung: Superior lobar artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to the superior lobe of the right lung.
superior medial genicular artery: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.
superior mesenteric artery: Arises from the aorta at L1 and passes in front of the 3rd part of the duodenum to supply the midgut (small intestine, ascending colon and 2/3 of the transverse colon). Its acute occlusion causes mesenteric ischaemia.
superior mesenteric vein: Drains the small intestine and right colon.
superior ophthalmic vein: Drains the orbit and opens into the cavernous sinus.
superior petrosal sinus: Connects the cavernous sinus with the transverse sinus.
superior phrenic arteries: Small branches from the thoracic aorta to the upper surface of the diaphragm.
superior sagittal sinus: In the upper border of the falx cerebri; the arachnoid granulations empty CSF into it.
superior segmental artery of left lung: Superior segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
superior segmental artery of right lung: Superior segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
superior thyroid vein: Drains the upper pole of the thyroid.
superior ulnar collateral artery: Accompanies the ulnar nerve and joins the anastomosis around the elbow.
superior vein of left lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
superior vein of right lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
superior vena cava: Formed by the two brachiocephalic veins and opens into the right atrium; compression by lung tumours causes superior vena cava syndrome.
supra-orbital artery: Supplies the forehead and the front of the scalp.
suprascapular artery: Passes above the superior transverse scapular ligament; joins the scapular anastomosis.
supratrochlear artery: Supplies the middle of the forehead; the pedicle of the forehead flap.
supreme intercostal artery: Supplies the first two intercostal spaces.
temporal branches of middle cerebral art: Temporal branches of middle cerebral artery
Supply the lateral surface of the temporal lobe.
temporo-occipital branch: Supplies the border between the temporal and occipital lobes.
thoracic aorta: Runs in the posterior mediastinum from T4 to the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm (T12); gives intercostal, bronchial and oesophageal branches.
thoraco-acromial artery: Pierces the clavipectoral fascia and gives pectoral, deltoid, acromial and clavicular branches.
thoracodorsal artery: Supplies latissimus dorsi; a free-flap pedicle.
thyrocervical trunk: Short trunk giving the inferior thyroid, suprascapular and transverse cervical arteries.
transverse cervical artery: Crosses the posterior triangle of the neck.
transverse facial artery: Supplies the parotid gland and the skin of the cheek.
transverse sinus: Sinus running from the confluence to the sigmoid sinus.
ulnar artery: Descends on the medial side of the forearm; passes through Guyon's canal to form the superficial palmar arch.
vertebral artery: First branch of the subclavian artery; rises through the transverse foramina of C6–C1, enters through the foramen magnum and joins its partner to form the basilar artery.
vertebral vein: Descends with the vertebral artery through the transverse foramina.
????????: Small venous segment opening into the coronary sinus.

Small branch of the artery of the pterygoid canal.
